content.abstract:
Multi-proxy Studies on Late Quaternary Lake
Sediments from Schirmacher Oasis, East Antarctica
Anupam Sharma, Amalava Bhattacharyya, Binita Phartiyal and
Sameer Kumar Bera
Birbal Sahni Institute of Palaeobotany, 53 University Road,
Lucknow 226 007, Uttar Pradesh, India
ABSTRACT
The ~35 km 2 land area of Schirmacher Oasis (SO) in east Antarctica is
occupied by over 100 and 150 lakes, respectively. Besides these lakes, there are
many other dried up lakes which contain sediments making them promising
archives for understanding surface geological processes, palaeoenvironment and
palaeoclimatic conditions.
High resolution sampling was carried out on several sites of SO during
26
th ISEA, 2006-07. Sediment samples were collected by using manual sediment
corer or by making pit/trench and also from exposed sections. In general, it was
observed that at all subsurface sampling locations in SO region, the permafrost
zone was encountered at a depth of ~80-85cm during the summer period. The
top most few centimeters of sediment profile is relatively coarse followed by
finer sediments wherein the sand, silt and clay distribution varies at different
intervals at different locations. A positive correlation is noticed between silt-clay
and moisture-organic carbon content in the samples. The bulk mineral composition
is dominantly comprised of quartz, feldspar, mica with accessory phases like
zircon, garnet, apatite etc. In clay fraction illite is the most abundant mineral.
The major and trace including rare earth element (REE)  distribution is largely
controlled by the grain size composition of the samples where larger grain size
is showing higher amount of quartz hence an increase in SiO
2 content also. With
decreasing grain size the concentration of Al, Fe, Mn, Mg and K although is
increasing but the increase in Al is very small indicating that clay mineral
formation process is not very effective, however, an increase in K and thereby
in Ba and Rb is supporting the illite formation. Relatively higher gain in Fe and
Mg suggests weathering of mafic minerals and retained by clay minerals in the
profile. An increase in Na and Ca content, in specific samples, is a result of
precipitation due to evaporation/drier conditions. The identical pattern of REE’s
suggests that the samples are well homogenized, however, the abundance varies
according to grain size i.e. larger the grain size lower is the abundance probably
due to ‘quartz dilution effect’.

The overall sediment characteristics suggest that the samples having
smaller grain size, higher moisture and organic content and also an increased
concentration of immobile elements is deposited under relatively warmer climatic
conditions when the water supply was relatively more which in turn helped the
weathering processes and organic activity. Contrary to this the cooler conditions
restrict the effectiveness of earth surface processes either by limiting the
exposed area and melt water supply or by reducing the depth of permafrost zone
in the region.
Besides, 42 lake water samples, ~35 airobiological samples and palynology
of a sediment profile is also carried out for understanding the earth surface
process, air circulation and climatic history of the region.
Keywords:  Antarctica, Schirmacher Oasis, Lake sediments, Mineralogy,
Geochemistry, AMS dates
INTRODUCTION
The Antarctica continent is known for the several superlatives viz.
it is the southernmost, coldest, loftiest, windiest continent containing the
largest pool of the global fresh water with thinnest biodiversity and
human population. The ~98% of the Antarctica continental surface
remains covered with ice throughout the year and only ~2% of it is
exposed for surface conditions commonly occurring as hills, nunataks,
massifs and oasis. Antarctica plays a pivotal role in determining the
ocean and atmospheric currents movements, which in turn control the
global climate, a better understanding of the region including the physical-
chemical-biological processes and their dynamics is always advantageous
more so when the region has experienced least human interventions and
could also be used as control due to its pristine environment.
Since the Antarctica continent is relatively very young to human
knowledge, the climatic instrumental records are merely a few decades
old and therefore other proxy records preserved in ice, lake sediments
and water bodies become important. Among all, the lake sediments
preserve an array of information related to earth surface processes such
as weathering and erosion, primary mineral disintegration/decomposition
and secondary mineral formation, elemental mobility and differentiation,
nutrient availability and productivity etc (Green et al. 2005; Sinha et al.
2003; Lyons et al. 2002; Sleewaegen et al. 2002; Green et al. 2001;
Sinha & Chatterji 2000; Webster et al. 1995; Ramteke et al. 1
